transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’ve felt this heavy, low mood every day for over a year, like I just can’t shake feeling down no matter what I do. It's like a constant weight that I carry around, and I just don't know how to get past it anymore.
Have you had any periods of at least 2 months during the past year when your mood felt normal or close to normal, or has the low mood been present כמעט every day without a break?

No, I haven't had any breaks or normal periods at all. This heavy, low mood has been there steadily every single day for over a year now. I haven't had even a single day, let alone two months, where I felt close to normal.
Along with the low mood, have you also had low energy, poor self-esteem, trouble concentrating, or changes in sleep or appetite most days?

Yes, I've been struggling with all of those. I barely sleep and wake up at 3 AM with my mind racing, I've lost a lot of weight because I have no appetite, and I constantly feel like a complete failure as a husband and father. On top of that, I have this heavy brain fog that makes it impossible to focus, and physically everything feels slowed down, like I'm wading through mud.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, thoughts of hurting yourself, or any plans to end your life?

Yes, especially late at night when I'm all alone, I catch myself thinking it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. I've actually gone as far as counting out my leftover pain pills, wondering if taking them all at once would finally let my family move on.
Have you made any actual plans to end your life, or taken any steps toward doing so, such as setting a time, writing a note, or gathering pills?

I haven't written a note or set a specific date, but counting out those leftover pain pills is the closest I've come to a plan. I just sit there with them in front of me late at night, seriously thinking about doing it, though I haven't gone through with it yet.

Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energetic or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, talked more than normal, or did risky things that were out of character for you?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. It's actually been the exact opposite for me—I just feel completely drained, incredibly slow, and low all the time.

How much has this low mood and loss of energy affected your ability to work, take care of yourself, and function in daily life? Have you been able to do your usual activities, or has it become very difficult or impossible?

It has completely derailed my life; I've gone from being a top performer at work to missing deadlines, falling behind on sales targets, and getting a warning from my boss because I keep calling in sick. Outside of work, I barely see my friends anymore and I can't even keep up with basic chores like doing laundry or paying my bills on time.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during this time when your mood and energy were back to normal, or has it been low nearly every day for the entire year without any breaks?
No, there have been absolutely no breaks or periods of feeling normal. This heavy mood and low energy have been completely steady every single day for the entire year, ever since my wife moved out.
Have you had this low mood and low energy for at least 2 years total, with symptoms present most days, or has it been closer to just over 1 year?

It’s been closer to just over a year, not two years. This heavy mood and low energy started steadily right after my wife took our son to stay at her sister's place, which was a little over a year ago.

No history of manic or hypomanic episodes is reported. Duration is over 2 years? No—only just over 1 year, supporting a severe depressive episode rather than persistent depressive disorder.
